newsitem.title: HONG KONG: U.S. diplomat in HK sees future lying with business.
newsitem.headline: U.S. diplomat in HK sees future lying with business.

text.p: Hong Kong's business community could exert the biggest influence in maintaining the territory's autonomy after its handover to China, the top U.S. diplomat in the British colony said on Friday.

"The attitudes and actions of Hong Kong's business community may do more than anything else to ensure that Hong Kong's autonomy is realised," U.S. Consul General Richard Boucher told the Chinese Manufacturers Association of Hong Kong.
Hong Kong reverts to China at midnight on June 30 after more than 150 years of British rule.

Beijing has promised Hong Kong a large degree of autonomy for 50 years after the handover, although there are concerns over changes the communist mainland may make to the territory's free-wheeling economy and way of life.

With 130 days to go until the change of sovereignty, Boucher said priorities included upholding Hong Kong's free trade stance, especially in international forums like the World Trade Organisation and the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation.

The United States has a vested interest in seeing Hong Kong maintain autonomy over its customs officers due to the territory's role as a major transshipment point for Chinese products, many of them destined for U.S. shores.
